Problem

POST /nadir/remove-tripod-payment validates size as min:50|max:100 (RemoveTripodPaymentController.php), but the FE nadir scale slider (PatchingNew.jsx) allows 10-100.

When a user drags the scale slider below 50 and submits an AI-generative nadir patch, BE rejects with 409 TOURS.VALIDATION_FAILED ("Invalid input") even though the value was valid in the UI.

History

min:50 was introduced in commit 7d0a5878b ("Create a New Worker ai_nadir_test for new version of ai_nadir", 2026-03-30), changed from the original min:10. FE slider range was never updated to match.

Fix

Align BE validation range with FE: change min:50 back to min:10 in
app/Http/Controllers/Tours/Nadir/RemoveTripodPaymentController.php.

Reference

  • FE slider: src/pages/Tour/Detail/Nadir/Components/PatchingNew.jsx:440-448 (gothru-dashboard repo)
  • BE validator: app/Http/Controllers/Tours/Nadir/RemoveTripodPaymentController.php:32

Result

Changed size rule to min:10|max:100 (was min:50), matching FE slider range — no other logic touched, no tests depended on the old value. Pushed to main @ 54b1b5bb2.

issues.display_title: Issue #1774: Handle Stripe 3DS for space addon subscription change
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Add Stripe 3D Secure (3DS) authentication handling to the space addon subscription-change endpoint (POST /v2/payment/subscription/space-addon), matching the existing Upgrade.php / CompleteUpgrade3DS.php pattern.

Current state

SpaceAddon.php calls $stripeClient->subscriptions->update() without payment_behavior or an expand on latest_invoice.payment_intent, and treats any non-active resulting subscription status as a hard failure:

if ($charged->status != 'active') {
    return ['status' => false, 'message' => 'Payment Failed, subscription not active', ...];
}

When the card on file requires 3DS authentication, Stripe leaves the subscription incomplete (not active) with no path back to the customer to complete authentication — the request just fails with a generic error and a failure email, even though the card itself is fine.

Target state

  • SpaceAddon.php sets payment_behavior: pending_if_incomplete + expand: ['latest_invoice.payment_intent'] on the subscription update, inspects pending_update / payment_intent->status, and when 3DS is required stashes the pending change to Redis ({userId}_space_addon_3ds_{clientSecret}, 24h TTL) and returns 202 with {status: "requires_action", client_secret} instead of failing.
  • New POST /v2/payment/subscription/complete-space-addon-3ds endpoint (CompleteSpaceAddon3DS.php) verifies the invoice is actually paid after the client completes 3DS, then runs the same user/plan update, cc_purchase insert, invoice generation, and success email the non-3DS path already runs.
  • Existing behavior for non-3DS cards is unchanged, including the ch_... charge-id resolution (fix(payment): use charge id for space addon) already in place on the sync path — must be preserved on both the sync and new 3DS-completion paths.

Scope

  • app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Stripe/Subscription/SpaceAddon.php — executeSpaceAddonChangePlan(), new private store3DSSpaceAddonDataToRedis().
  • app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Stripe/Subscription/CompleteSpaceAddon3DS.php (new).
  • app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Stripe/SubscriptionControllerV2.php — new spaceAddonComplete3DSV2().
  • routes/billingRoutes.php — new POST /complete-space-addon-3ds route.

Out of scope

  • /subs, /upgrade, /downgrade, Upgrade.php, CompleteUpgrade3DS.php — already handled, not touched.
  • Reusing/generalizing CompleteUpgrade3DS.php to also cover space addon — isolated endpoint pair instead.
  • Any change to how productId (18 monthly / 19 yearly) is derived.
  • Failure email on /complete-space-addon-3ds error paths — matches CompleteUpgrade3DS.php, which also sends nothing on failure.

Risk / test plan

  • No automated test suite covers Stripe action classes in this module (StripeClass instantiates the Stripe SDK directly, no DI seam) — php -l plus manual verification is the bar, same as Upgrade.php/CompleteUpgrade3DS.php. tests/Actions/Payment/SpaceAddonTransactionIdTest.php covers the charge-id resolution specifically and must stay green.
  • Manual QA in Stripe test mode: /space-addon with a 3DS test card → 202 requires_action → confirm 3DS client-side → /complete-space-addon-3ds with the same client_secret → 200, space_addon updated, cc_purchase row with ch_... transid, invoice generated, success email sent.
  • Manual QA: /complete-space-addon-3ds with a pi whose invoice isn't paid yet → 409, no email, no cc_purchase row.
  • Manual QA: /space-addon with a non-3DS test card → still completes synchronously, unchanged.

Implemented in #1773.

Create the "Notify New Invoice" email template in the Plunk dashboard per the GoThru Email Payment Template doc, then register its UID in code.

Current state

Target state

Doc content, section "Notify New Invoice":

  • Subject: "Your Invoice is Now Available!"
  • Body: greets customer by name, informs invoice is ready, link to invoice file labeled "View Invoice"
  • Variable: {customer_name}
  • Footer: standard GoThru contact info (phone, YouTube, Facebook)
  • Trigger: sent when a new invoice is generated

Template exists live in Plunk with the above subject/body/variable, and EmailTemplateUID.php has a NOTIFY_NEW_INVOICE constant with its UID, added to getAllUIDs(), getUIDByName(), getNameByUID().

  • app/Constants/EmailTemplateUID.php: add NOTIFY_NEW_INVOICE constant + mapping entries.

Out of scope

  • Wiring the new UID into an actual EmailClass->send() call site (no code path currently generates/sends this on invoice creation — separate task).
  • All other templates from the doc.

Risk / test plan

issues.main_description_html:
Problem

POST /test-reset-subscription resets local DB subscription fields but does not cancel Stripe subscriptions whose IDs start with sub_.

Current behavior:

  • Authenticates user by Authorization token.
  • Sets users.space_addon = 0, users.space_addon_plan = null, users.subscribtion = 0.
  • If user_extra_data.recurring_profile starts with I-, cancels PayPal subscription.
  • Clears user_extra_data.recurring_profile, current_recurring_plan, check_space.
  • Deletes unsubscribes rows.
  • Does not cancel Stripe subscription IDs in recurring_profile.

This can leave active Stripe test subscriptions detached from GoThru accounts.

Fix

  • Match /test-reset-photo-studio-subscription behavior and block non-test users with HelperClass::isUseStripeTestMode().
  • If recurring_profile starts with sub_, cancel it through Stripe test client before clearing DB fields.
  • Keep PayPal I- cancellation behavior.
  • Return proper status codes using HelperClass::getStatusCode(), not always 409.

Acceptance

  • Test user with recurring_profile=I-* still cancels PayPal subscription.
  • Non-test user gets 403 and no DB mutation.
  • Existing local reset behavior remains unchanged after successful cancellation.

Result

issues.display_title: Issue #1781: Research: document cancel_users_account.php cancellation/failed-payment flow
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Research task to document the actual business flow behind cancel_users_account.php (the cron that reacts to failed recurring charges) and produce a gap/strength assessment of the current implementation vs. intended GoThru billing policy.

Current state

  • No documented spec exists for how cancel_users_account.php decides a payment has failed or what it's supposed to do in response.
  • An initial code-only read (not yet validated against actual business intent) found:
    • Three divergent branches — PayPal DirectLink status check, Stripe/Verisign recurring-profile status check, and the manual/queued unsubscribes (unsubscribe_type=1) processor — that each write a different subset of users, user_extra_data, unsubscribes, affiliates_program, and users_cc_renewal_dates.
    • get_stripe_all_trans.php and cc_purchase_complete.php log and then filter out failed charges, but neither feeds into this cron — the cancellation decision is made by re-querying the gateway live, not from logged data.
  • None of this has been confirmed against what GoThru's billing policy is actually supposed to be.

Target state

A short written doc (place under the repo's existing spec/notes convention — see the pattern used for #1778) that answers:

  1. What is GoThru's intended policy on a failed recurring charge — grace period, immediate downgrade, dunning emails, retry count? (Get this from whoever owns billing, not just from the code.)
  2. Does the current code match that policy, per gateway (Stripe subscription, Stripe customer, PayPal DirectLink, Verisign recurring profile)?
  3. Concrete gap list, each confirmed intentional or bug, e.g.: affiliates_program.pay_active and users_cc_renewal_dates.subscribed are only updated on user-initiated cancel (unsubscribe_type=1), never on auto-cancel from a failed charge (unsubscribe_type=2).
  4. Concrete strengths worth preserving, e.g. the unsubscribes pending-request guard in the RP/Stripe branch that stops a user mid-grace-period from being double-cancelled.
  5. Confirm or dismiss two defects found in the initial read: the dead condition at get_stripe_all_trans.php:89 (checks $val['respmsg'], but the key actually set is respm, so the branch never fires), and the live Stripe secret key hardcoded in plaintext, duplicated across get_stripe_all_trans.php, cc_purchase_complete.php, and cancel_users_account.php.

Scope

  • gothru.co/cancel_users_account.php
  • gothru.co/get_stripe_all_trans.php
  • gothru.co/cc_purchase_complete.php
  • Tables: users, user_extra_data, unsubscribes, affiliates_program, users_cc_renewal_dates, cc_logs, cc_logs_stripe, cc_purchase
  • Confirm intended behavior with whoever owns billing/subscription business rules.

Out of scope

  • No code changes in this task — research and documentation only. File separate implementation issues once gaps are confirmed as real bugs to fix.

Risk / test plan

N/A — research task. Deliverable is a written doc, reviewed and confirmed against actual GoThru billing policy rather than tested as code.

Result

Full write-up: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-14-cancel-users-account-cron-research.md

  • 6 independent branches in cancel_users_account.php, no single cancellation path — trigger + writes mapped for each.
  • Both suspected defects confirmed: dead respmsg condition at get_stripe_all_trans.php:89, and the hardcoded live Stripe key (4x in this file's immediate family, 40+ across gothru.co overall).
  • Live Stripe data pulled with a new read-only tool (php artisan payment:check-stripe-dunning) confirms the real grace window: 21-day/5-attempt dunning, then a further ~9-10 days until Stripe auto-cancels, then up to 1 day cron lag — 3+ weeks minimum, no cap, and the user keeps full paid access the entire time.
  • 10 confirmed gaps total, including zero customer email during the whole dunning window, an email-subject leak between branches, overlay-deactivation code that's commented out while the email still claims it ran, and a PayPal-legacy manual-cancel path that skips the confirmation email entirely.
  • Billing-policy questions (grace period acceptability, downgrade-vs-hard-cancel intent, per-gateway policy) are still open, flagged for the billing owner in the doc.

No code changes made — per scope, will file separate implementation issues once gaps are confirmed as real bugs to fix.

issues.display_title: Issue #1794: Record PayPal recurring transactions cronjob
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

PayPal-equivalent of #1764: a cronjob endpoint that records PayPal recurring subscription renewal payments into the legacy billing tables, the same way RecordStripeRecurringTransactionsHelper does for Stripe.

Current state

Stripe recurring renewal charges are now logged via /record-stripe-recurring-transactions (#1764, PR #1760): each renewal charge is written to cc_logs_stripe, and a deduped cc_purchase row is inserted when the charge succeeded and a user_id was resolved. PayPal REST API subscriptions (CreateSubscription.php) have no equivalent — renewal payments on PayPal subscriptions are not being logged to cc_logs_paypal or cc_purchase anywhere in the API codebase.

Note: #1471 already tracks a broader PayPal cronjob (porting the legacy PayFlow Pro script get_paypal_link_trans.php and covering REST API subscriptions). This issue scopes out just the REST API recurring-renewal slice, mirrored 1:1 against the Stripe implementation, so it can ship independently of the PayFlow Pro migration.

Target state

  • Fetch PayPal subscription renewal payments for the cronjob window and log every attempt to cc_logs_paypal.
  • Insert a deduped cc_purchase row for successful renewals when a user_id can be resolved.
  • Resolve user_id from user_extra_data.recurring_profile / recurring_profile_photo_studio — same column Stripe uses; PayPal subscription IDs (I-...) are stored there too (see CreateSubscription.php), so the resolution tier is identical to RecordStripeRecurringTransactionsHelper::resolveUserId().
  • Resolve product_id the same way the sync PayPal subscribe flow does (PaypalHelper::convertProductNameToId() / plan-to-product mapping — check CreateSubscription.php for the exact source).
  • Dedup purchase inserts by PayPal capture/transaction id.
  • Support ?test_mode=1 against PayPal sandbox, matching the Stripe cronjob's manual-verification pattern.

Open design question — how to enumerate renewal payments

Stripe's helper does one polling call (charges.all with a created range) across the whole account. PayPal REST has no direct equivalent:

  • Option A — per-subscription polling: loop every active PayPal recurring_profile in user_extra_data, call GET /v1/billing/subscriptions/{id}/transactions?start_time=&end_time= for each. Simple, no extra scopes, but O(n) calls per run.
  • Option B — Transaction Search API: GET /v1/reporting/transactions returns all account transactions (including subscription payments) in one paginated call, closer to the Stripe charges.all shape — but requires the Transaction Search product/scope to be enabled on the PayPal app; confirm this is available before committing to it.
  • Option C — webhooks: subscribe to PAYMENT.SALE.COMPLETED / BILLING.SUBSCRIPTION.PAYMENT.FAILED and log on receipt instead of polling. Real-time, but it's a webhook handler, not a cronjob — bigger shape change from the Stripe pattern and needs its own reconciliation story for missed events.

Whoever picks this up should confirm which option is viable against the current PayPal app config before implementing.

Scope

  • routes/cronjobRoutes.php — add the cronjob route (e.g. record-paypal-recurring-transactions).
  • app/Http/Controllers/Cronjobs/CronjobController.php — wire the endpoint, following recordStripeRecurringTransactions() as the template.
  • app/Http/Controllers/Cronjobs/Helpers/RecordPaypalRecurringTransactionsHelper.php — orchestrate payment fetch, filtering, logging, user/product resolution, and purchase insert.
  • app/Http/Controllers/Cronjobs/Helpers/PaypalRecurringChargeRules.php — isolate the recurring-cycle and purchase-recording decision rules, mirroring StripeRecurringChargeRules.
  • app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Helpers/Paypal/PaypalHelper.php — add whatever fetch method the chosen option (A/B/C above) needs.
  • api-collection/GoThru API NEW/Cronjob/Record Paypal Recurring Transactions.yml — add Bruno/manual API entry.
  • tests/Helpers/Cronjobs/PaypalRecurringChargeRulesTest.php — cover the pure decision rules.

Out of scope

  • Legacy PayFlow Pro migration (get_paypal_link_trans.php) — tracked separately in #1471.
  • Backfilling historical recurring payments.
  • Changing existing synchronous subscribe, upgrade, downgrade, Stripe, or non-subscription purchase flows.

References

  • Stripe implementation: app/Http/Controllers/Cronjobs/Helpers/RecordStripeRecurringTransactionsHelper.php, StripeRecurringChargeRules.php (#1764, PR #1760)

Summary

A PayPal subscription payment succeeded on PayPal's side, but local DB writes stopped halfway: user_extra_data/users were updated, while cc_logs + cc_purchase + invoice were never written. There is no PayPal webhook / retry / reconciliation mechanism, so this gap stays permanent without manual repair.

Case data (user 29546 — femiomomo@gmail.com)

  • Aug 22, 2026 02:59 UTC: PayPal sub I-E1WXUVCTDW1R ACTIVE (plan P-7GL25033FK647912VNF43F3I)
  • Aug 22, 2026 03:25 UTC: payment $75 COMPLETED, transaction ID 1G49172999430860H
  • DB state before repair:
    • ✅ recurring_profile = I-E1WXUVCTDW1R, current_recurring_plan = 'prov', users.subscribtion = 5
    • ❌ No cc_logs row with processor paypal for that transaction
    • ❌ No cc_purchase row, no invoice PDF, no success email

Repair already done (manual)

Backfilled via php artisan paypal:backfill-payment 29546 I-E1WXUVCTDW1R (new command: BackfillPaypalPayment.php):

  • 1 cc_logs row (trxtype R, transid 1G49172999430860H, processor paypal, $75.00)
  • 1 cc_purchase row (product_id 16, profile_id I-E1WXUVCTDW1R)
  • Timestamps UTC+0, verified in DB (log_id 107574). Invoice will be auto-generated from cc_purchase.

Result — findings & remediation plan

Findings based on the original incident (user 29546):

Findings

  1. Swallowed errors in best-effort logging — insertCCPurchaseForUpgrade is wrapped in a try/catch that only does error_log("cc_purchase/invoice failed:") (UpgradeHandler.php:437-454). Any failure in cc_logs / cc_purchase / invoice generation disappears silently.
  2. Silent early-return — if billing info lookup returns empty, postUpdateBestEffort returns without any log (UpgradeHandler.php:409-411).
  3. Partial writes without rollback — core user DB is written first, transaction logging runs afterwards as best-effort, with no DB transaction and no retry. Failure mid-way produces exactly this incident: user data ✅ but cc_logs/cc_purchase ❌.
  4. No safety net after payment succeeds — refund/cancel compensation only triggers for failures before the DB update; there is no PayPal webhook or reconciliation to detect/repair gaps.

Remediation plan (separate tasks to be created)

  • Replace swallowed error_log calls with structured Log::error + alerting
  • Never silently early-return on missing billing info — at minimum log a structured warning
  • Wrap DB writes in a single transaction, or add an outbox/retry mechanism so logging gaps self-heal
  • Reconciliation cron: compare COMPLETED PayPal transactions vs cc_purchase, auto-backfill missing rows

Summary

Extend GET /cronjob/process-unsubscribes-table to also detect genuinely-failed PayPal REST API recurring subscriptions and queue them for cancellation (Phase 1 PayPal), reusing the existing provider-agnostic UnsubscribesSweeper (Phase 2, unchanged).

PayPal does not auto-cancel a subscription on failed renewal (unlike Stripe) — a failed payment just leaves it SUSPENDED. This closes that gap.

Spec

docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-28-paypal-unsubscribes-detection-design.md

Decisions

alphabetically business_name A-Z

Field Type Source Notes

page int page query Optional; default 1, minimum 1

type string type query Optional tour-type filter
search string search query Optional keyword filter
sortBy string sort_by query Optional; unsupported values use default sorting
encrypt bool enc header Optional; default true

  "data": {

issues.display_title: Issue #1815: Investigate and Fix Invoice Generation Failure for user_id=6516
issues.main_description_html:
Description:

Diagnose why the automated billing/invoice pipeline failed to produce the latest invoice record for user_id=6516 following their recent payment cycle.

Acceptance Criteria:

  1. Inspect payment gateway webhook logs (e.g., Stripe, PayPal, or Chargebee) for user_id=6516 to trace unhandled webhook events or failed database insertion transactions.
  2. Fix the root cause preventing invoice record creation and manually regenerate the missing invoice for user_id=6516.

🛠️ Developer Update & Notes

Root Cause Analysis (Previous Logic):

The legacy cronjob logic strictly relied on a -24 hours rolling time window. This approach was unreliable and caused missing invoice/transaction records due to:

  1. Dunning Period / Retried Charges: When an initial Stripe charge failed and was successfully retried after the 24-hour cutoff, the transaction was never captured.
  2. Execution/Network Failures: If a cron execution failed or timed out, any transaction within that 24-hour window was permanently skipped and never re-evaluated once the time window passed.

Resolution & New Implementation:

  • Replaced the time-window query with a cursor-based active subscription polling model (chunk_size=100) iterating over active profiles in user_extra_data.
  • For each subscription, the cron retrieves the last 5 invoices/charges (limit=5) directly from Stripe.
  • Deduplication against cc_purchase (transid) ensures safe idempotency.
  • Optimized database load by making cc_logs_stripe insertions insert-if-not-exists (skipping redundant updates on old immutable records).
  • Scheduled to run on a 10-minute crontab interval.

Results:

  • Executed 1 full live backfill cycle across all active subscriptions (10 chunks / 908 subscriptions).
  • Successfully backfilled and recorded 87 missing transactions into cc_purchase (including user_id=6516), generated invoice PDFs, and dispatched notification emails.
  • Execution history and cursor state are tracked in Redis (gothru:cron:record-stripe-recurring:log).
